reason: The text primarily portrays the elders of Israel (זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), who constitute the local elite leadership, in a favorable manner. The passage concludes with the elders believing God's word, listening to Moses, and worshiping (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ...וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃). While Egyptian taskmasters (נֹגְשָׂ֔יו) are mentioned negatively as oppressors, they are not portrayed as 'the elite' but rather as functionaries. The Egyptian king is mentioned only as the target of a diplomatic request and is not characterized unfavorably in this passage.
